pr_title: cdc: add detail to buffer closed error
pr_body:
When a kvfeed closes the buffer it's writing to due to an expected error,
such as a schema change, the reader may return ErrBufferClosed before the
error has propagated to be available to the caller of Get(), leading to a
race condition. Rather than force the caller to wait for an error it knows
is coming, we can decorate the ErrBufferClosed with the reason.

Fixes #71796
Fixes #71797 
Fixes #72019

Release note (bug fix): Fixed a race condition that could have caused core changefeeds whose targeted table became invalid to not explain why when shutting down.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/72490)

___ *[pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/changefeed_processors.go, line 447 at r1](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/72490#-Mo02DzXEM2lHA2VLeWA:-Mo0KhPPE9iPz2bQ3uSe:b-y6tq0a) ([raw file](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/c4f7087787d0fbef4e665699cb527520faba85eb/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/changefeed_processors.go#L447)):*
Previously, miretskiy (Yevgeniy Miretskiy) wrote…
Should we consider changing `ErrBufferClosed` from being a sentinel error to being a "true" error w/ additional methods? Something like: ``` type ErrBufferClosed struct { reason error } // ... other methods required for error interface func (e ErrBufferClosed) IsRestartRequested() bool { ... } ``` then here we could do something like: `if e := (*ErrBufferClosed)(nil); errors.As(err, &e) && e.IsRestartRequested() ....1
That did seem more natural to me but I was nervous about how that would work with marshalling in mixed versions; would I need to keep both the error type and the old sentinel error around?

> That did seem more natural to me but I was nervous about how that would work with marshalling in mixed versions; would I need to keep both the error type and the old sentinel error around?

Do we ever marshal that error? change frontier detects these things by watching frontier.  Afaik, we never serialize this error message in any way...
I think the build failures here are now just the ones we're also seeing intermittently on master, although it's hard to be sure. Ready for re-review.

comments:
@HonoreDB This feels similar to the issue you fixed in ca07d9bf5714a0e205b912fb77a1446ac7c4f19d. But, it has me a bit nervous.  If this is a similar situation where we see a duplicate, why are we suddenly seeing them more often now? That we see a duplicate at all is rather surprising given how simple the test setup is.  

Also given the TruncateOrDrop test failed last night (that https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/71797) perhaps something else is afoot?

I think the bug is here https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/master/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/kvfeed/kv_feed.go#L117 

I don't think we should be closing the writer in that case. 
 Right now closing the writer is a signal that we are shutting down with an error that the changeAggregator will detect itself (a schema change).  I think we broke it here: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/commit/3e0a94429d7ec6286dfe690c101f685f57f0eb74#diff-3adb512d3390cf29b3e69f8fa5d1196a733174e5b72a32f0c97436c9054e1dceR117

@miretskiy Right exactly. Previously we were only ever closing it in the schema change case. The schema change case is going to generate an error on the changeAggregator side.  When I said we should not be closing the writer, I meant with the assumptions in the code in changeAggregator. I think we can clean up change aggregator so closing this buffer is always correct though.

Agree that this is probably the same issue as what _actually_  caused the test failure that prompted ca07d9bf5714a0e205b912fb77a1446ac7c4f19d (your theory seems plausible). It's interesting that all three test failures have been in sinkless.

Note that these failures are with `TAGS=deadlock`, so running under stress with the deadlock detector, which was introduced earlier this week. Since this has additional overhead, it makes timing-sensitive flake more likely to trigger.
